question: Florida real estate license applicants who are subject to Level 2 background screening under Chapter 435, F.S., have their fingerprints checked against which of the following?
choice_a: Statewide criminal history records through FDLE, national records through the FBI, and local law enforcement records
choice_b: Only county-level arrest records in the applicant's county of residence
choice_c: Credit history records maintained by national credit bureaus
choice_d: Civil litigation records maintained by the Florida court clerks only
explanation: Section 435.04, F.S., defines Level 2 screening as including fingerprinting for statewide criminal history checks through the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, national criminal history checks through the FBI, and local criminal records checks through local law enforcement, plus a search of sexual predator/offender registries for states of recent residence.

question: Under Section 475.25(1)(f), F.S., a real estate license may be denied, suspended, or revoked based on a conviction, guilty plea, or nolo contendere plea to a crime that:
choice_a: Directly relates to the activities of a broker or sales associate, or involves moral turpitude or fraudulent or dishonest dealing
choice_b: Involves any traffic infraction, regardless of severity
choice_c: Occurred more than 20 years before the application, regardless of nature
choice_d: Was committed exclusively outside the United States
explanation: Section 475.25(1)(f), F.S., authorizes discipline (and is applied to background review of applicants) for a conviction or plea to a crime -- in any jurisdiction, and regardless of adjudication -- that directly relates to real estate license activities or involves moral turpitude or fraudulent or dishonest dealing.

question: A Florida real estate licensee who pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is convicted or found guilty of, any felony must inform the commission of that fact in writing within what time period?
explanation: Section 475.25(1)(p), F.S., makes it a separate disciplinable offense for a licensee to fail to inform the commission in writing within 30 days after pleading guilty or nolo contendere to, or being convicted or found guilty of, any felony -- a distinct duty from the general change-of-address notification requirement.

question: Florida real estate broker and sales associate licenses operate on a biennial renewal cycle with two staggered expiration groups. On what dates do these licenses expire?
choice_a: March 31 and September 30 of odd-numbered years
choice_b: January 1 and July 1 of even-numbered years
explanation: DBPR assigns real estate licensees to one of two biennial renewal groups expiring March 31 or September 30 of odd-numbered years; renewal requirements (fees and applicable education) must be completed by midnight Eastern time on the assigned expiration date.
source_note: DBPR Real Estate Commission Licensure Information page (renewal cycle)

question: To qualify for a Florida real estate instructor permit to teach FREC-prescribed prelicensing or exam-preparation courses, an applicant must satisfy one of several qualification paths, including which of the following?
choice_a: Hold a bachelor's degree in a business-related subject and a valid Florida broker's license, or pass a commission-approved instructor's examination
choice_b: Hold only a high school diploma and five years of sales experience
choice_c: Be a currently licensed sales associate with no degree requirement at all
choice_d: Complete only the 72-hour broker prelicensing course
explanation: Section 475.451, F.S., allows an instructor permit applicant to qualify by holding a bachelor's degree in a business-related field plus a valid Florida broker's license, by holding a bachelor's degree plus extensive real estate experience plus a valid broker's license, or by passing a commission-approved instructor's examination.

question: To renew a Florida real estate instructor permit, the permit holder must show proof of completing a minimum of how many hours of instruction in real estate subjects or instructional techniques?
explanation: Section 475.451, F.S., requires an instructor permit holder to complete a minimum of 7 classroom or distance-learning hours of instruction in real estate subjects or instructional techniques as a condition of permit renewal, separate from the CE hours required of active brokers and sales associates.

question: Under Section 455.02, F.S., a Florida real estate licensee who is an active-duty member of the U.S. Armed Forces is entitled to which licensure accommodation?
choice_a: The license is kept in good standing without paying renewal fees during active duty and for up to 2 years after discharge, and the renewal fee is waived
choice_b: Automatic upgrade from sales associate to broker status upon deployment
choice_c: Permanent exemption from all future continuing education for life
choice_d: A requirement to re-take the licensing exam upon return from active duty
explanation: Section 455.02, F.S., provides that an active-duty service member's professional license is kept in good standing without fees during active duty and for 2 years following discharge, and the department must waive the license renewal fee for a member engaged in the profession for profit.
source_note: Section 455.02, F.S. (military service member licensure accommodations)

question: Under Section 455.02, F.S., a military spouse who holds a valid real estate license issued by another state and relocates to Florida due to a service member's active-duty orders is entitled to:
choice_a: Licensure by endorsement with the initial application fee waived, and issuance within 7 days of a complete application
choice_b: No accommodation; the spouse must complete the full 72-hour prelicensing course like any other applicant
choice_c: A permanent Florida license requiring no renewal, ever
choice_d: Automatic reciprocity only if the prior state is one of Florida's 10 mutual recognition states
explanation: Section 455.02, F.S., entitles a military spouse holding a valid out-of-state professional license to licensure by endorsement, with the initial licensure application fee waived and the department required to issue the license within 7 days after receiving a complete application -- separate from and broader than the mutual recognition program.
source_note: Section 455.02, F.S. (military spouse licensure by endorsement)

question: Under Section 475.011, F.S., which of the following is exempt from Florida real estate licensure requirements when acting within the scope of employment?
choice_a: An employee of a public utility, rural electric cooperative, railroad, or state or local governmental agency
choice_b: An unlicensed assistant who negotiates lease terms on a landlord's behalf for a fee
choice_c: A mortgage broker acting as a dual agent
choice_d: A licensed home inspector who also lists properties for sale
explanation: Section 475.011, F.S., exempts an employee of a public utility, a rural electric cooperative, a railroad, or a state or local governmental agency from real estate licensure requirements when acting within the scope of that employment -- a distinct exemption category from the attorney-at-law exemption.

question: Under Section 475.011, F.S., a salaried employee of an apartment community's owner (or of a registered broker acting for that owner) who works in the property's onsite rental office is exempt from licensure for which specific activity?
choice_a: Renting apartment units in that community
choice_b: Listing and selling the entire apartment complex to a third-party investor
choice_c: Negotiating the sale of individual condominium units to the public
choice_d: Managing a commercial office leasing portfolio across multiple properties
explanation: Section 475.011, F.S., exempts a salaried employee of an apartment community owner (or of a broker registered for that owner) who works from an onsite rental office from licensure requirements, but only for renting units in that community -- not for sales activity.

question: Under Section 475.011, F.S., an owner who sells their own property directly is exempt from real estate licensure requirements EXCEPT when:
choice_a: The owner employs compensated agents to sell the property to the public in the ordinary course of business
choice_b: The property is sold for more than $500,000
choice_c: The property is located outside the owner's county of residence
choice_d: The sale takes place more than 60 days after listing
explanation: Section 475.011, F.S., exempts owners selling their own property, but the exemption does not extend to situations where the owner employs compensated agents to handle transactional sales of that property to the public in the ordinary course of business.

question: Under Section 475.15, F.S., a partnership, LLC, or corporation that registers with the commission to act as a real estate broker will have its registration automatically canceled if:
choice_a: The license or registration of at least one active broker member of the entity is not in force
choice_b: The entity changes its business address without notifying DBPR
choice_c: Any sales associate affiliated with the entity lets continuing education lapse
choice_d: The entity's annual gross sales fall below a statutory threshold
explanation: Section 475.15, F.S., provides that a brokerage entity's (partnership, LLC, or corporation's) registration is automatically canceled if the license or registration of at least one active broker member of that entity is not in force.

question: Under Section 475.15, F.S., if the sole broker of a registered brokerage entity dies or unexpectedly becomes unable to remain the broker, Florida law allows for:
choice_a: The commission to register a broker for the brokerage on a temporary, emergency basis
choice_b: Immediate and permanent dissolution of the brokerage entity with no recourse
choice_c: Automatic transfer of the broker's license to the highest-producing sales associate
choice_d: A mandatory 1-year waiting period before any broker may be registered for the entity
explanation: Section 475.15, F.S., directs the commission to adopt rules allowing a brokerage to register a broker on a temporary, emergency basis when the sole broker of that brokerage dies or unexpectedly becomes unable to remain a broker, so the entity's registration is not automatically lost.

question: Under Section 475.161, F.S., a broker associate or sales associate may be licensed as a professional corporation, LLC, or professional LLC only if:
choice_a: The licensee provides the commission with authorization from the Department of State for that entity
choice_b: The licensee has held an active license for at least 10 years
choice_c: The entity is registered as a general partner of a brokerage firm
choice_d: The broker associate simultaneously holds a separate broker's license
explanation: Section 475.161, F.S., provides that a broker associate or sales associate is licensed as an individual by default, in the licensee's legal name, unless the licensee provides the commission with authorization from the Department of State to be licensed as a professional corporation, LLC, or professional LLC.
source_note: Section 475.161, F.S. (individual vs. professional entity licensing)

question: In addition to being at least 18 years old, what other baseline personal qualifications does Section 475.17, F.S., require of a Florida real estate license applicant?
choice_a: Hold a high school diploma or its equivalent, and be honest, truthful, trustworthy, and of good character
choice_b: Hold a bachelor's degree in any field
choice_c: Have prior employment in a sales-related occupation
choice_d: Be a U.S. citizen with at least 2 years of Florida residency
explanation: Section 475.17, F.S., requires applicants to be at least 18 years old, hold a high school diploma or its equivalent, and be honest, truthful, trustworthy, and of good character -- separate personal-qualification requirements from the SSN/identification requirement.

question: Under Section 475.17, F.S., which applicants are exempt from the standard pre- and post-licensing education requirements for real estate licensure?
choice_a: Applicants holding a 4-year degree, or higher, in real estate from an accredited institution
choice_b: Applicants who have worked in any sales occupation for at least 10 years
choice_c: Applicants who are licensed attorneys, regardless of practice area
explanation: Section 475.17, F.S., exempts an applicant who holds a 4-year degree, or higher, in real estate from an accredited institution from the pre- and post-licensing education requirements otherwise imposed on license applicants.
source_note: Section 475.17, F.S. (education exemption for real estate degree holders)
